count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.d: A node is 'good' if no node on the path from the root to it has a greater value. Count the good nodes.
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree.i: DFS passing down the maximum value seen on the path so far; a node is good if node.val >= that max.

count-number-of-bad-pairs.d: A pair (i, j) with i < j is bad if j - i != nums[j] - nums[i]. Count the bad pairs.
count-number-of-bad-pairs.i: Rearrange: a pair is GOOD when nums[i] - i == nums[j] - j. Count good pairs with a HashMap of (nums[k] - k) frequencies, then bad = n(n-1)/2 - good. Use long.

count-submatrices-with-top-left-element-.d: Count the submatrices that include the top-left cell (0,0) and whose sum is <= k.
count-submatrices-with-top-left-element-.i: Every such submatrix is a prefix rectangle (0,0)..(i,j). Build the 2-D prefix sum P[i][j] = g[i][j] + P[i-1][j] + P[i][j-1] - P[i-1][j-1] and count cells with P <= k.

course-schedule.d: There are numCourses courses and prerequisite pairs [a, b] meaning b must be taken before a. Can all courses be finished?
course-schedule.i: It's possible exactly when the prerequisite graph has no cycle. Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take nodes with in-degree 0; if every node gets taken, there is no cycle.

course-schedule-ii.d: Same setup as Course Schedule, but return a valid order to take all courses, or an empty array if impossible.
course-schedule-ii.i: Kahn's algorithm: the order nodes leave the queue is a topological order. If fewer than numCourses are output, there's a cycle.

customer-placing-the-largest-number-of-o.d: From an Orders table, return the customer_number with the most orders (exactly one such customer).
customer-placing-the-largest-number-of-o.i: GROUP BY customer, ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, LIMIT 1.
k: GROUP BY + ORDER BY count + LIMIT

customer-who-visited-but-did-not-make-an.d: Find customers who visited without making a transaction and how many such visits each had.
customer-who-visited-but-did-not-make-an.ex: customer 54 had 2 visits with no transaction -> (54, 2)
customer-who-visited-but-did-not-make-an.i: Keep visits whose visit_id is NOT IN the Transactions table (or LEFT JOIN and test for NULL), then GROUP BY customer.

daily-temperatures.d: For each day, return how many days until a warmer temperature (0 if none).
daily-temperatures.i: Monotonic stack of indices (next greater element). Scanning right to left, pop indices whose temperature is <= today's; the top is the next warmer day.
k: Monotonic decreasing stack, right to left

decode-ways.d: Digits map to letters (1->A ... 26->Z). Count the ways to decode a digit string.
decode-ways.i: ways(i) = ways(i+1) if s[i] != '0', plus ways(i+2) if s[i..i+1] is between 10 and 26. A '0' can never start a code.

delete-node-in-a-linked-list.d: Delete a given (non-tail) node from a singly linked list without access to the head.
delete-node-in-a-linked-list.i: You can't reach the previous node, so copy the next node's value into this node and unlink the next node: node.val = node.next.val; node.next = node.next.next. (Your version shifts every later value; the one-step version is O(1).)
k: Shift values forward and drop the tail

delete-operation-for-two-strings.d: Return the minimum number of single-character deletions (from either string) to make the two strings equal.
delete-operation-for-two-strings.i: Whatever survives is a common subsequence, so keep the longest one: answer = len1 + len2 - 2 * LCS.

design-twitter.d: Design a mini Twitter: postTweet, follow, unfollow, and getNewsFeed returning the 10 most recent tweets from the user and the people they follow.
design-twitter.i: Store each user's tweets newest-first with a global timestamp. For the feed, merge k sorted lists with a max-heap: push each followee's newest tweet, pop and push that user's next tweet, 10 times.
k: K-way merge with max-heap (lazy, push next tweet)
Push all candidate tweets into a size-10 min-heap

diameter-of-binary-tree.d: Return the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes of a binary tree.
diameter-of-binary-tree.i: While computing heights bottom-up, the longest path bending at a node is leftHeight + rightHeight; keep the maximum in a global variable.

distinct-subsequences.d: Count how many distinct subsequences of s equal t.
distinct-subsequences.i: f(i, j) = ways using s[0..i) to form t[0..j). If s[i-1] == t[j-1]: use it (f(i-1,j-1)) or skip it (f(i-1,j)); else only skip. Base: f(i,0)=1, f(0,j>0)=0.

distribute-candies.d: Alice may eat n/2 of her n candies. Return the maximum number of distinct candy types she can eat.
distribute-candies.i: Answer = min(number of distinct types, n/2). Count types with a HashSet.
k: HashSet of types, min with n/2

distribute-elements-into-two-arrays-i.d: Put nums[0] in arr1 and nums[1] in arr2; each next element goes to arr1 if arr1's last element is greater than arr2's, else to arr2. Return arr1 followed by arr2.

duplicate-emails.d: Report every email that appears more than once in the Person table.
duplicate-emails.i: GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1. (HAVING filters groups; WHERE filters rows.)

eat-pizzas.d: Eat exactly 4 pizzas per day. On odd days you gain the heaviest of the four, on even days the second heaviest. Maximise total weight gained.
eat-pizzas.i: Sort. Odd days (ceil(days/2) of them) take the largest pizzas outright. Even days each need two big pizzas and gain the smaller of the pair, so take every second pizza from what remains at the top. Fill each day with the smallest pizzas.

edit-distance.d: Return the minimum number of single-character inserts, deletes or replaces needed to turn word1 into word2.
edit-distance.i: f(i, j): if chars match, f(i-1, j-1); else 1 + min(insert f(i, j-1), delete f(i-1, j), replace f(i-1, j-1)). Base: f(i,0)=i, f(0,j)=j.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.d: Evaluate an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish (postfix) notation, with integer division truncating toward zero.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.i: Push numbers onto a stack; on an operator pop b then a (order matters for - and /), push a op b.
